cards.heading: Copper UTP
cards.body: Twisted-pair copper (UTP) with RJ-45 connectors reaches 100 m. Cat 5e handles 1 Gbps, Cat 6a 10 Gbps. Twisting the pairs cancels interference.

cards.heading: Straight-through, crossover and Auto-MDIX
cards.body: PCs, routers, servers and APs transmit on pins 1,2; switches and hubs transmit on 3,6. Unlike devices use a straight-through cable; like devices need a crossover. Auto-MDIX on modern ports detects and corrects the wrong cable. A rollover cable connects a console port.

cards.heading: Fiber
cards.body: Fiber carries light, so it's immune to electrical interference and goes much further. Multimode fiber (wide core, cheaper optics) covers hundreds of metres; single-mode fiber (narrow 9 µm core, lasers) covers kilometres. Common connectors are LC and SC, usually in an SFP module.

cards.heading: Shared media and point-to-point
cards.body: Old hubs made one shared collision domain where only one device could send at a time (half duplex, CSMA/CD). Switch ports are point-to-point: each link is its own collision domain and runs full duplex, so collisions shouldn't happen at all.

cards.heading: Reading show interfaces
cards.body: The first line gives the layer 1 / layer 2 status. 'administratively down' = shut down. 'down/down' = no physical link. The counters show symptoms: runts (frames under 64 bytes), giants (over 1518), CRC errors (corrupted frames), collisions and late collisions.
cards.example:
Fa0/1 is up, line protocol is up (connected)
  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s
     312 runts, 0 giants
     4810 input errors, 4497 CRC

cards.heading: Duplex and speed mismatch
cards.body: If one end is hard-coded and the other is auto, the auto end senses the speed but falls back to half duplex (at 10/100). The half-duplex end sees late collisions; the full-duplex end sees CRC errors and runts. A speed mismatch keeps the link down. Fix: configure both ends the same, ideally auto.

cards.heading: Other symptoms
cards.body: CRC errors with matching duplex point at a damaged cable, a cable over 100 m or interference. err-disabled means a feature (port security, BPDU Guard) shut the port; fix the cause, then shutdown / no shutdown.
